goal: Find a practical way to reduce false freezer-temperature alarms in a food bank while still catching genuine warming events.
hard_constraints: One technician has four days and can inspect two existing sensors and archived minute-level temperatures; no new hardware purchase.
Food may not be deliberately warmed and alarm coverage may not be disabled during staffed or unstaffed hours.
Distinguish sensor placement, door-opening transients and sensor drift; include a check that a proposed change does not mask a true sustained excursion.
available_resources: Two spare calibrated thermometers and staff door-opening notes.
expected_result: A reversible diagnosis and mitigation with a small validation plan.

goal: Plan a safe migration of a small nonprofit's 12,000 contact records from two inconsistent spreadsheets into one database without silently merging different people.
hard_constraints: Two staff members have ten workdays, local spreadsheet and SQLite tools, and no paid matching service.
Original files must remain untouched; every merge must be reversible and provenance retained.
Do not expose private contact data in reports; define checks for missed duplicates and wrongful merges.
available_resources: Local sample review of at most 150 ambiguous pairs.
expected_result: An implementable migration workflow and acceptance checks.

goal: Diagnose intermittent vibration in one of six identical ventilation fans before a planned maintenance shutdown.
hard_constraints: A mechanic has one week, a handheld vibration meter, existing maintenance logs and one 30-minute shutdown window.
Do not open energized housings or stop all ventilation simultaneously.
Distinguish imbalance, loose mounting and bearing wear without claiming a cause from one noisy measurement; state a safe escalation trigger.
available_resources: Five healthy fans as comparators and a spare mounting kit.
expected_result: A prioritized diagnostic sequence and repair decision.

goal: Reduce missed updates in a volunteer-run community calendar where events arrive by email and printed flyers.
hard_constraints: Three volunteers share a free spreadsheet and have no authority to change senders' habits.
No event may be published without date, place and source confirmation; corrections must be traceable.
Keep weekly upkeep under two hours and avoid collecting attendee names.
available_resources: Existing inbox, flyer tray and a static public calendar page.
expected_result: A low-maintenance intake and verification process with an error audit.

goal: Design a fair test to determine whether a new biodegradable packing insert protects fragile ceramic mugs as well as the current insert.
hard_constraints: A workshop has 60 mugs, a basic drop rig, and 30 inserts of each type; no shipment of intentionally damaged goods.
Account for variation in mug batches and drop orientation; define damage criteria before testing.
Include a stopping rule for excessive breakage and do not claim equivalence from a nonsignificant result.
available_resources: Two staff and a camera for recording test outcomes.
expected_result: A feasible comparative test and decision rule.

goal: Make a small clinic's appointment reminder process more reliable when text messages sometimes fail, without increasing privacy exposure.
hard_constraints: Use existing scheduling software export and a staffed phone line; no new vendor or patient app.
A reminder must not reveal clinical details, and opt-outs must be honored.
Two clerks have 30 minutes daily; distinguish bad phone numbers, delivery failure and response failure; report how missed appointments and unwanted contact would be measured.
available_resources: Aggregate delivery status and existing consent records.
expected_result: An operational fallback workflow with privacy and workload checks.

goal: Teach 16 middle-school students to interpret a chart with a truncated vertical axis and explain how it changes a visual claim.
hard_constraints: One 40-minute class, printed charts and a whiteboard; no devices.
Do not require students to disclose grades or personal experiences.
Include an individual transfer question on an unseen chart and a criterion that distinguishes noticing the axis from explaining the effect.
available_resources: Teacher can print two contrasting charts per student.
expected_result: A timed lesson and check for transferable graph interpretation.

goal: Help adults in a community workshop compare the total cost of two household energy plans with different fixed and usage charges.
hard_constraints: One facilitator has 50 minutes, calculators, paper and no live pricing access.
Use fictional prices and avoid recommending a real provider.
Mixed numeracy levels must have a meaningful participation route; assess a new usage scenario individually, including a crossover case.
available_resources: Printed fictional bills and rate cards.
expected_result: A practical comparison activity and individual decision check.

goal: Train new museum volunteers to distinguish observation from interpretation when describing an unfamiliar artifact.
hard_constraints: A 30-minute session for eight volunteers with photographs and no access to the original object.
Do not invent the artifact's provenance or historical function.
Participants need to practice saying what remains unknown; assess an unseen image individually rather than only group discussion.
available_resources: Three unlabeled artifact photos and a facilitator.
expected_result: A repeatable micro-lesson and observation rubric.

goal: Teach beginner gardeners to decide when to water seedlings using soil evidence rather than a fixed daily habit.
hard_constraints: A 35-minute indoor session with pots, soil, water and paper; no electronic moisture meter.
Avoid overwatering live shared seedlings during practice.
Include a dry/wet ambiguous case and an individual transfer decision with a reason and a follow-up observation.
available_resources: Prepared sample pots at different moisture levels.
expected_result: Hands-on activity and a safe decision check.

goal: Help first-time library volunteers handle a disagreement about a shared room booking without taking sides prematurely.
hard_constraints: A 45-minute training with role cards and one facilitator.
Do not ask trainees to recount personal conflicts; no legal or disciplinary advice.
Practice must include verifying the booking record, listening to both parties, and knowing when to escalate; assess an unseen scenario individually.
available_resources: Fictional booking records and policy excerpt.
expected_result: A role-play sequence and actionable escalation check.

goal: Teach 20 adult learners to spot when a recipe scaling calculation changes cooking time assumptions, not just ingredient quantities.
hard_constraints: One 40-minute classroom session with printed recipes and no kitchen or devices.
Avoid food allergy disclosures or real food preparation.
Assess a new scaling scenario individually, requiring a safe test or observation rather than an invented fixed cooking-time formula.
available_resources: Fictional small and large batch recipe cards.
expected_result: A clear lesson with transfer assessment and uncertainty handling.

goal: Create an optional two-minute interaction that helps people notice overlooked textures in a public garden.
hard_constraints: Two volunteers have three weeks, weatherproof printed material and permission for a freestanding sign only.
No touching plants, collecting visitor details, power or phone requirement.
Usable from a seated position and worthwhile for someone passing quickly; pilot against a plain information sign without claiming results.
available_resources: Existing garden map and volunteer observation shifts.
expected_result: A specific low-cost interaction and pilot signals.

goal: Design a recurring shared reading ritual for residents of a small apartment building that works even if only a few people participate.
hard_constraints: A committee has a lobby shelf, paper and four weeks; no resident directory, app or public ranking.
Do not collect identifiable reading histories or require book purchases.
Participation must remain optional and accessible to residents who cannot stand at the shelf; define a two-week feasibility pilot.
available_resources: Donated public-domain short texts and volunteer check-ins.
expected_result: A repeatable ritual, privacy safeguards and observable pilot checks.

goal: Invent a small traveling exhibit that invites children and adults to compare how everyday objects are repaired across generations.
hard_constraints: One curator has six weeks, three display cases and existing donated objects with uneven documentation.
No fabricated provenance, live tools, electrical power or mandatory phone interaction.
Objects must stay protected; every interaction needs a seated and low-reading alternative; test against ordinary labels.
available_resources: Object photos, repair notes where documented, printable cards.
expected_result: A feasible exhibit concept and critique plan.

goal: Make a neighborhood walking route feel welcoming to newcomers without directing people to private homes or making local claims that cannot be checked.
hard_constraints: A community group has one month, a printed map and permission to mark only three public stopping points.
No paid app, GPS tracking, photography of participants or required group meeting.
Route must have a short accessible option and a safe bad-weather fallback; pilot for clarity and exclusion.
available_resources: Public-space descriptions and volunteer route inspection.
expected_result: A route mechanic and practical pilot.

goal: Create a low-pressure way for a repair café to celebrate failed repair attempts as useful learning rather than shame.
hard_constraints: Four volunteers have a table, paper and a small display board for one monthly event.
No photos or names without explicit consent, no prizes or leaderboards, and no unsafe repair advice.
Participation is optional, usable without public speaking, and does not slow the queue substantially; pilot with observation and opt-out checks.
available_resources: Existing repair notes with permission to summarize anonymously.
expected_result: A concrete ritual and evaluation of learning versus embarrassment.

goal: Design a quiet, repeatable activity for a train-station waiting area that lets travelers notice sounds without adding noise.
hard_constraints: One arts group has printed cards, a freestanding display permit and two weeks to prepare.
No recording, microphones, speakers, power, phone requirement or collection of personal information.
Do not block circulation; readable from a seated place, optional in under two minutes, and test against a plain poster.
available_resources: Station-approved display location and short volunteer observation periods.
expected_result: A specific silent interaction with accessibility and upkeep checks.
